title: Add a whole show in one press

items.title: No season to choose
items.text: If someone already has a show here, Add to library now adds every episode they have straight away, across all seasons. To get anything else, press More episodes.

items.title: Ranges say what they're doing
items.text: A download of part of a season now shows which episodes are coming and how many are skipped, instead of looking like the whole season.

items.title: Ask for more episodes later
items.text: Asking for other episodes of a season uses the batch already on the server when it can, and skipped episodes now really start downloading.

items.title: Remove a show that's still downloading
items.text: You can now remove a show from your library while it's still downloading, and it stays gone. If someone else asked for it too, it carries on for them.

items.title: See how far it's come
items.text: The TV now shows progress wherever something's on its way: on the home screen, on a title's page, beside each episode and on cards in Discover. It tells you how many episodes are ready, too.

items.title: A home for documentaries
items.text: Discover has a new Documentaries tab, and it's on the TV's home screen too. Browse true crime, serial killers, unsolved cases, Swedish and Nordic documentaries, history, nature, science, music, sport and many more.

items.title: Free from SVT Play
items.text: SVT Play's documentaries and true crime are here now. Press Add and it lands in your library with Swedish subtitles, ready on every screen. Titles that the torrent sites don't have can often come from SVT Play instead. It only works in Sweden.

items.title: Better at finding things
items.text: Search looks in one more big source, and Swedish names with å, ä and ö find their releases more often. Search results also show what's on SVT Play.

title: See your downloads on the TV

items.title: On its way, in the library
items.text: Something you add on the TV now shows in your library straight away, in an On its way row with how far along it is. It moves to Films or Shows when it's ready.

items.title: Go to library
items.text: After you add a title on the TV, a Go to library button takes you straight to it.

items.title: Only what's in your library
items.text: Someone else's downloads no longer notify you about a show that isn't in your library, even if you follow it. Shows you have in your library still tell you about new episodes, and your own downloads still tell you when they're ready.

items.title: Choose your language
items.text: Marquee now speaks English and Swedish. Pick under Settings → Language and it applies everywhere: menus, the player, messages and notifications, on every device you sign in on. Descriptions and genres follow too, while titles keep their names.

items.title: One TV app, in Swedish
items.text: The new TV app with Discover, Search and genres has replaced the old one. It's in Swedish, and the on-screen keyboard has å, ä and ö.

items.title: Subtitles written by people come first
items.text: Marquee now always picks subtitles written by people when they exist. When only a machine translation exists, the language says “auto-translated” so you know what you’re getting, and it’s replaced automatically once people’s subtitles turn up.

items.title: Ready before you press play
items.text: When new episodes arrive or a season is upgraded, Marquee now finds their intros and credits in the background, so Skip intro and Up next are less likely to turn up late the first time you watch. Upgraded episodes also keep what was already found.

items.title: Fewer subtitles missed
items.text: The subtitle list could miss a language when a title had many subtitles in common languages. It now finds them. A language still only appears when someone has made subtitles in it for what you're watching.

items.title: Add instead of Download
items.text: Getting something new is now just Add: on a film, a show, a season or a single episode. If it's already here it's ready right away; otherwise it shows as On its way, then Almost ready, until you can press Play. A show you already watch says More episodes instead.

items.title: Georgian and Tagalog subtitles
items.text: Georgian and Tagalog are now in the subtitle list, next to the other languages, wherever someone has made them for what you're watching.

items.title: Proper episode titles
items.text: While an episode plays, the top of the player now shows the show's name and the episode's real title, like "House · Season 3, Episode 2: Cane & Able", instead of a short code like "house S03 E02".

items.title: Versions instead of double cards
items.text: If a film or an episode is here in two qualities, say 4K and 1080p, it now shows as one title instead of two. A Quality choice on the film's page, the season's page and in the player's quality menu picks which one plays. Your place carries over between them, on the website, TVs and Jellyfin. Phones start with the lighter version unless you pick another; your choice is remembered on each device.

items.title: No more accidental second copies
items.text: Downloading a film or episode you already have in the same quality is refused, with what's already here. Releases in a quality you have are marked in the release list. Another quality is fine: it becomes a version. A season pack only downloads the episodes you don't already have in that quality.

title: Better picture, and an Upgrade button

items.title: Best Quality means best picture
items.text: With Download quality set to Best Quality, Marquee used to pick the most popular release, and that is often a tiny re-encode that looks soft on a big screen. It now looks at how much picture a release really has (its size for the resolution, where it came from and who made it), so you get a proper BluRay or web release when one is out there. Balanced also skips releases that are far too small for their resolution.

items.title: Upgrade quality
items.text: Got a season that looks bad? Open Download on the show, pick the season and press Upgrade quality. Marquee looks for a clearly better release, downloads it, and swaps each episode for the new one as soon as it has finished. Your place in each episode carries over. If nothing better is out there, it tells you.

items.title: Names and I/l mix-ups fixed
items.text: Some releases come with subtitles that were read off the disc by a computer, so names and abbreviations show up in lowercase ("cuddy", "nicu") and I and l get swapped ("ls there", "l'm"). Marquee now fixes these in English subtitles as you watch, on the website, TVs and casting. It learns how names are spelled from the other subtitles in the library, so it gets better as the library grows.

items.title: Episodes 150 to 200
items.text: Long seasons (40 episodes or more, like Black Clover or One Piece) now have an Episodes choice in the Download panel. Pick "Choose a range", type the first and last episode, and only those download. A whole-season batch can still be used: the episodes outside your range are simply skipped.

items.title: One Piece numbering
items.text: One Piece's episodes keep their real numbers (Wano is episodes 892 to 1088), so downloads, the library and the episode list all agree. Searches no longer mix up the anime with the 2023 live-action series.

title: Stuck episodes no longer block a season

items.title: Seasons keep downloading
items.text: When a few episodes of a season can't find anyone to download from, the rest of the season now carries on instead of waiting behind them. A whole-season download also goes ahead of single episodes it already includes.

items.title: Anime downloads from Nyaa
items.text: Marquee now also searches Nyaa, where anime is released. Download Season on an anime picks a whole batch (one download for a season, even 170 episodes) instead of one torrent per episode, and finds single episodes whichever way they're numbered: "Black Clover - 176", "Black Clover 2nd Season - 06" and "S02E06" are all the same episode now.

items.title: Anime seasons line up
items.text: Anime that TMDB counts differently (Frieren's two seasons are one on TMDB, Jujutsu Kaisen's three seasons too) lands on the right season and episode in your library, under its proper name, and Marquee knows which episodes you already have so nothing downloads twice.

items.title: Subtitles on by default
items.text: If you've never picked subtitles, anime turns on the English subtitles it came with, so Japanese audio isn't left untranslated. Pick another language or Off in the player and that sticks as before.

items.title: Watch your library in Jellyfin
items.text: Got your own Jellyfin? Install the Marquee plugin there, open its settings and enter the code it shows under Settings → Jellyfin here. Your films and shows then appear in every Jellyfin app, and what you watch there shows up in Continue watching here too.

items.title: A lighter stream for big files on your phone
items.text: 4K films and other very large files used to stutter on phones. Now, on a phone, Marquee plays them as a lighter 1080p stream made on the fly, so they start fast and play smoothly, also on mobile data. The original file on the server stays exactly as it is.

items.title: Pick the quality yourself
items.text: The new quality button in the player (on phones and tablets) lets you choose Auto, Original, 1080p or 720p (a data saver). Your choice is remembered, and switching keeps your place in the video.

title: Browse and search on the TV (Preview)

items.title: A bigger Discover in Marquee Preview
items.text: In the Marquee Preview TV app, Discover rows now keep loading as you move along them, end in See all (a full grid), and are followed by a row of genres and one row per genre. Films / Shows tabs at the top narrow it down, and the title you're on fills the top of the screen with its description. Genre pages can be sorted by Popular, Top rated or Newest.

items.title: Search and genres on the TV
items.text: Marquee Preview has a Search screen with an on-screen keyboard (a real keyboard works too): your own titles show up at once, everything else from TMDB a moment later. Your library on the TV now also has a row for each genre you own something in.

items.title: Play on TV keeps your subtitles
items.text: Play on TV now starts with the same subtitles the player would turn on for you (your last language, or the one in Settings), so you don't have to pick them again in the TV remote. If they can't be fetched, the video starts without them. Apple TV still can't show subtitle files over AirPlay.

title: Player hints out of the way

items.title: Volume, sleep timer and skip hints
items.text: The little messages in the player (volume, sleep timer, skips, night mode and so on) now show just above the middle of the picture, so they no longer cover the play button or the loading ring on your phone. The play/pause flash stays in the middle, on the play button.

title: Agents can tap you on the shoulder

items.title: Notifications from your agents
items.text: A script or AI agent on your home machines can now send you a notification when it needs you. It uses the House token and only works from the home network. Turn it off under Settings › Notifications › Agents.

title: Browser copies can't fill a drive

items.title: Cache on any drive
items.text: The new CACHE_DIR setting in .env puts browser copies, timeline previews and share copies on a bigger drive than Marquee's own folder.

items.title: A cap and a safety margin
items.text: Browser copies stay under 150 GB (BROWSER_COPIES_MAX_GB); the ones nobody has watched for longest make room first. Conversions also leave 20 GB free on every drive (MIN_FREE_GB) and wait instead of filling it.

items.title: One library for the household
items.text: The owner can now let several people share one library. Everyone in it sees the same films and shows, on the TV too, and anyone can add, keep or remove titles. Your watch progress stays your own.

items.title: Set it in People
items.text: Settings → People has a Library choice for each person: Own library, or share with someone (joining someone who already shares joins the whole group).

items.title: Quieter library
items.text: The "Preparing playback" bar now only appears for videos in your library, and only when your browser actually needs that copy to play them. If you can already watch it, you won't see it.

items.title: Two conversions at once
items.text: Marquee now makes the quick copy for iPhone and Apple TV and the slower copy for older browsers at the same time, instead of one after the other. A new film no longer waits behind another film's long conversion.

items.title: Full quality in more browsers
items.text: If your browser plays HEVC (most do now, including Firefox on many PCs), you always get the original picture. The re-encoded copy is only used by browsers that can't play it.

title: Skip intro and Next episode on the TV

items.title: On your phone's TV remote
items.text: When you play an episode on the TV, the remote on your phone now shows Skip intro while the opening plays, and Up next once the credits start. Next episode starts it on the TV, with the same 10-second countdown as on the phone. Keep the remote open for the countdown: a locked phone can't start the next one.

items.title: Says what it's converting for
items.text: Some new films get a second, one-time copy that plays in every browser. The banner at the top of the library now says that, so it no longer looks like the same film is being converted twice. You can watch while it runs.

items.title: Trailers on title pages
items.text: Open a film or show in Discover and press Trailer on the picture at the top. The trailer plays right there, and stops when you close the page.

items.title: Adult content is blocked
items.text: Marquee no longer downloads porn. It's left out of torrent search, and links or .torrent files for it are refused. If a download turns out to contain it once it starts, it's removed straight away.

items.title: See who's sharing
items.text: Download details now show how many seeders a download is connected to, out of how many exist, like "12 of 340 seeders". The dot is lit when plenty are sharing and empty when nobody is, so you can tell a slow download from a stuck one.

items.title: Scroll with arrows
items.text: Continue watching in Library now has ← → buttons next to its title, like the rows in Discover. They only show when there are more cards than fit on screen.

items.title: Close stays in reach
items.text: The ✕ on sheets like this one now stays in the corner while you scroll, instead of scrolling away with the text.

items.title: Cleaner bottom edge
items.text: In What's new, text no longer peeks out below the Got it / Close button.

title: Faces, and a new Watch Together

items.title: Add your picture
items.text: Settings: tap the circle next to your name to add a profile picture. Drag it into place, zoom, save. It shows wherever your name does: Liked by, Popular on Marquee, watch parties, room chat and Wrapped.

items.title: Watch Together, redone
items.text: The room now opens as a panel beside the picture on bigger screens (a sheet on phones): everyone's face with a gold ring once they're ready, the host's crown, chat bubbles, one-tap invites with faces, and quick countdown buttons for the host. Invites look like a ticket and show who's already there.

items.title: Pictures for the family
items.text: In Settings → People, tap someone's circle to give them a picture (right-click to remove it).

items.title: Invite links work again
items.text: Since the sign-in update, opening an invite link and pressing Get access showed “This request came from another website”. That's fixed: invites you already sent work as they are.

items.title: Marquee Setup for Windows
items.text: Setting Marquee up on Windows no longer needs a terminal. Marquee Setup (in the Start menu, or MarqueeSetup.exe from the release page) walks you through your library, network, sign-in, services and start at boot, and checks your keys and ports as you go.

items.title: Game clips as an add-on
items.text: Turn on Clipper on the Game clips page: Setup installs it on this PC, or gives you one command to paste on your gaming PC and shares the clips folder for you.

items.title: Marquee in lights
items.text: Marquee has a new icon when you add it to your phone's home screen: a lit-up marquee M. On Android it now fills the icon shape properly instead of sitting in a white circle. Already added Marquee? Remove it from your home screen and add it again to get the new icon (iPhones keep the old one until you do).

items.title: Take it with you
items.text: Going somewhere without Wi-Fi? Open a film or episode and press To phone (the phone button on episode rows). Marquee makes a small copy (Small 480p, about 450 MB an hour, or Standard 720p) that plays in your phone's own video player with subtitles built in. Or download the file at full quality.

items.title: A whole season
items.text: Season to phone makes every episode of the season you're looking at. They're listed under For your phone in the Library, each with its own Download button as it's ready. With notifications on, you hear when one is done.

items.title: Phone copies
items.text: Copies are made one at a time with the GPU when it has NVENC, kept in cache/travel for 7 days after their last download (TRAVEL_KEEP_DAYS) and capped at 50 GB (TRAVEL_MAX_GB). HDR is tone-mapped to SDR.

items.title: Scrubbing looks the part
items.text: The picture you see while hovering or dragging along the timeline now sits in a small velvet card with the time in marquee gold, and a little pointer shows exactly where you'll land. While a preview is still loading, the card keeps its size instead of jumping.

items.title: Thumbs up, thumbs down
items.text: Rate any film or show from its page. Everyone sees who liked something ("Liked by Anna and Ben"); a thumbs down stays private.

items.title: Popular on Marquee
items.text: A new row near the top of Discover shows what people here liked and watched lately.

items.title: Chat and reactions in Watch Together
items.text: Open Room while watching together to send emoji that float over the picture, or chat. Messages pop up over the video, even with the controls hidden.

items.title: Plan a watch party
items.text: Pick a time from a film's or episode's page (the people icon) and send the invite. Everyone gets a countdown, and playback starts by itself for whoever's in the room. Your parties wait in Library. The host can also start a running room with a short countdown.

items.title: Marquee Wrapped
items.text: Settings → Marquee Wrapped tells the story of your year: hours watched, top titles, your show of the year, your busiest days and who you watched with. It counts from today on.

items.title: Your own password
items.text: Marquee can now sign you in by itself. If the owner made you an account, you'll see a sign-in page when you're away from home, and Settings lets you change your password or sign out.

items.title: Safer from other websites
items.text: Marquee now ignores requests that other websites try to send through your browser, so a page you visit can't start downloads or delete anything.

items.title: Server security
items.text: Create sign-ins with node setup.js user add EMAIL. Visitors from the internet always sign in; HOME_NETWORK_ACCESS=signin makes people at home sign in too. On Windows, run node setup.js service install once in an admin PowerShell: it removes the old SYSTEM watchdog task. Clipper installs are now pinned and checksum-verified.

items.title: Hear when it's ready
items.text: Turn on notifications in Settings and your phone or computer tells you when a download is ready to watch, even with Marquee closed.

items.title: New episodes
items.text: When a new episode of a show you follow or have in your library arrives on Marquee, you'll get a heads-up. Each kind of notification can be switched off on its own.

items.title: Invite people to watch
items.text: In a Watch Together room, tap Invite and pick someone: they get a notification that opens the room.

items.title: On iPhone
items.text: Apple only allows notifications for apps on the Home Screen: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen, and turn notifications on from there.

items.title: Save for later
items.text: Press Save on any film or show to keep it in a Saved for later row at the top of Discover.

items.title: Download when it's out
items.text: Saved a film that isn't out yet? Tick "Download it when a good copy is out" and it downloads by itself once it's released, never a cinema recording.

items.title: Follow a show
items.text: Press Follow on a show and each new episode downloads by itself once it has aired. Episodes you already had aren't fetched again, and older episodes are left alone.

items.title: New and Coming up
items.text: Episodes that arrived this way show a New badge on the show until you open it, and the Library has a Coming up row with the next episodes and release dates.

items.title: Skip the opening titles
items.text: A Skip intro button now appears while a show's opening titles play (or press S). Marquee finds the theme song by comparing an episode with its neighbours, so it works even after a long cold open.

items.title: Or skip them automatically
items.text: Settings → Watching → Intros can skip openings on their own. Rewind into one and it plays as normal.

items.title: Night mode
items.text: Tap the moon in the player (or press N) to even out loud explosions and quiet dialogue, with voices lifted so you can keep the volume down.

items.title: Sleep timer
items.text: Also under the moon: pause after 15 minutes to an hour and a half, with the sound fading out gently, or at the end of the episode so the next one doesn't start while you sleep.

items.title: Subtitles your way
items.text: The subtitles menu now sets the style (a dark box, a soft shadow or an outline) and how high the lines sit, as well as the size.

items.title: Two languages at once
items.text: Pick a Second language in the subtitles menu to show it above the first. Handy for learning a language, or when you're watching with someone who reads another.

items.title: What's new, right here
items.text: From now on, Marquee shows you what changed after each update, just like this. You can read past updates any time in Settings → What's new.

items.title: Next episode starts with the credits
items.text: When the credits roll, an Up next card counts down and plays the next episode. Pause or tap Keep watching to stay where you are.

items.title: Stats for nerds
items.text: Press I while watching, or right-click the picture, to see everything about the stream: resolution, codecs, HDR, bitrate, dropped frames, buffer and download speed. Copy puts it all on your clipboard.

items.title: Previews while you seek
items.text: Drag along the timeline to see a small picture of that moment before you let go.

items.title: Subtitles that line up
items.text: Subtitles are checked against the audio and fixed when they drift, even when they were made for a different cut of the film.

items.title: Always up to date
items.text: Finished downloads, deletions and where you stopped watching on another device now show up straight away, without reloading.

items.title: Add to library
items.text: If someone else already has a title on the server, Download becomes Add to library: it's yours instantly, with nothing to wait for.

items.title: Exact clip cuts
items.text: Game clips can now be cut on any frame, not just the nearest keyframe, with no loss in quality.

title: Episode pictures and a tidier library

items.title: A picture for every episode
items.text: Episodes now show a still from the episode itself in the season list, Continue watching and Up next, so you can spot the one you want at a glance.

items.title: Delete a season or a whole show
items.text: A show's page can remove one season or the whole show in one go, instead of episode by episode.

items.title: Ready to play sooner
items.text: New downloads are prepared for playing about twice as fast, and Firefox gets its own copy straight away instead of when you press Play.

items.title: Tidier subtitles
items.text: Subtitle lines no longer crowd into each other, and long lines stop wrapping too early in Firefox.

items.title: Steadier TV casting
items.text: Play on TV keeps playing the file it started with, even if the library changes underneath it.

items.title: Notes on your phone
items.text: Notes fit small screens now: easy-to-tap actions with undo, the keyboard no longer covers what you're typing, and images open full screen.

items.title: Search inside images
items.text: Text in note images (screenshots, receipts, posters) is read automatically, so a search finds them too.

items.title: Notes and clips in Discord
items.text: A shared note shows as a preview card in Discord with its images or video. Shared clips open in Marquee's own player, at full quality.

items.title: Better clip editing
items.text: Cut several parts out of a clip in one edit, and leave out audio tracks you don't want, like a noisy mic.

items.title: House: Sharing and Screen Time
items.text: House → Sharing shows what streams and encodes cost the server right now. Screen Time shows how long each computer at home has been used, and on what.

items.title: Download in one press
items.text: Download picks the best release for you from your quality setting, size limit and audio language. For a show, choose the season and press Download Season.

items.title: Episodes in order
items.text: Episode one downloads first and at full speed, so you can start watching while the rest of the season finishes.

items.title: 1440p
items.text: Between 1080p and 4K, there's now a 1440p choice for sharp pictures without 4K's size.

items.title: One library
items.text: Downloads show on the title's own card in your library, episode by episode, as soon as each one is ready.

items.title: A library that keeps itself current
items.text: New downloads and changes appear in the library on their own, and when an episode ends, Marquee offers the next one.

items.title: Notes
items.text: A shared Notes tab for messages, links, photos and videos. Photos and videos uploaded from a phone stay private to Marquee.

items.title: Rename clips
items.text: Give a clip a proper name instead of the recorder's timestamp.

items.title: Your own account
items.text: Everyone signs in to their own Marquee: your library, where you stopped and your settings are yours. If someone else already has a title on the server, add it to your library instead of downloading it again.

items.title: Settings
items.text: A Settings tab for colour themes, default subtitles, preferred quality, the page Marquee opens on and how your library is sorted.

items.title: Watch Together
items.text: Start a room from the player and send the link: playback stays in sync for everyone, and each person picks their own subtitles. Links show a preview in Discord.

items.title: Shows by season
items.text: Shows appear once in your library with their seasons and episode names. When there's no good season download, Marquee gets it episode by episode.

items.title: Library clean-up
items.text: Videos leave your library 7 days after they finish downloading unless you tap Keep, so old downloads don't pile up on the server.

items.title: Arrows on Discover
items.text: Rows on Discover have arrows, so you can scroll them with a mouse.

items.title: House
items.text: The House tab shows the server's disks, downloads and services, plus the computers at home. Wake the gaming PC and pick Linux or Windows, or restart it into the other.

items.title: Clips
items.text: Game clips from the PC, grouped by game, with share links that play right inside Discord. Trim them without losing quality, or delete the ones you don't want.

items.title: Invite links
items.text: Make a one-time invite link in Activity: the person enters their email and gets access, no dashboard needed.

items.title: New player controls
items.text: A seek bar that shows how much has loaded and the time under your finger, volume that's remembered, and everything in one row. On phones, double-tap left or right to skip 10 seconds.

items.title: Subtitles that make room
items.text: Subtitles are sized to the picture and move just far enough to clear the controls while they show. On an upright phone they sit in the empty space below the picture.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text: Space to pause, arrows to skip and change volume, F for fullscreen, C for subtitles and more. Press ? while watching to see them all.

items.title: Pause or remove downloads
items.text: Downloads can be paused, resumed or deleted from their card.

items.title: Plays in Firefox
items.text: Browsers that can't play HEVC video, like Firefox, get a copy they can play, made automatically.

items.title: Subtitles fix themselves
items.text: Subtitles are lined up with the audio automatically when they're out of sync.

items.title: Nudge subtitles
items.text: If a line still shows up early or late, shift the subtitles in small steps from the player.

items.title: Safari and iPhone
items.text: Videos now play in Safari on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

items.title: Theater mode
items.text: In theater mode the player bar hides itself and the video sits in the middle of the screen.

items.title: One remote
items.text: When you cast to a TV, the remote shows only on the device that started it.

items.title: Activity log
items.text: The owner can see what happened on the server: who watched, downloaded and deleted what.

items.title: AirPlay and Chromecast
items.text: Send a film or episode to your TV at full quality.

items.title: Home TVs stay at home
items.text: The TVs at home are only offered when you're on the home network.

items.title: Ready sooner
items.text: New downloads are picked up for playing every 30 seconds instead of every two minutes.

items.title: Welcome to Marquee
items.text: Find films and shows, download them to the server and stream them in your browser, on any device.
